title: Dialysis — EHR Downtime — Prescription Verification

transcript.speaker: Beth Kowalczyk, RN
transcript.text: CNO, it's Beth Kowalczyk at the Outpatient Dialysis Center. Eleven patients are scheduled to start at 08:00. Their prescriptions and last labs are in the EHR. The 05:15 downtime viewer printout is in front of me. Three of them have new dry weights since Friday—confirmed by the nursing note in the EHR, but not on the paper form. I can start on time using the viewer data and call the nephrologist to confirm the changes. Or I can hold and wait for IT to restore the system. What do you advise?

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Beth, start on time. Use the 05:15 viewer data as the prescription source. Call the nephrologist for the three changed dry weights—get a verbal confirmation. Two clinicians must verify every machine setting against the paper flowsheet. Anyone whose prescription can't be confirmed waits for the provider. Page me if there's a conflict.

instructorNote: This inject tests the CNO’s authority to permit care under downtime. Watch for hesitation to act, or over-reliance on IT for clinical decisions. The CNO must assert trust in the downtime viewer and enforce verification.
